articles.title: Redações de universidades dos EUA são mais fáceis do que as do Enem? | G1
articles.standfirst: Após os candidatos precisarem escrever uma redação sobre a valorização do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) no Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) 2026, no domingo (8), uma comparação com temas de redações para o ingresso em universidades dos Estados Unidos viralizou nas redes sociais.
articles.summary: Comparação com temas de redações para o ingresso em universidades dos Estados Unidos viralizou nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
Temas de redações para ingresso em faculdades americanas são comparados com temas do Enem. — Foto: Reprodução

Qual conselho um dente do siso te daria? Pode parecer uma pergunta que beira o absurdo ou que faria parte de uma grande brincadeira de imaginação. Mas essa foi uma das propostas de redação para ingresso na Universidade de Chicago, em 2022/2023.

Após os candidatos escreverem uma redação sobre a valorização do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) no Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) 2026, no domingo (8), uma comparação com esse e outros temas de redações para o ingresso em universidades dos Estados Unidos viralizou nas redes sociais.

➡️Em um post no X, uma brasileira colocou lado a lado propostas do Enem dos últimos anos com o que foi exigido por faculdades como a Universidade de Chicago.

Em 2018, por exemplo, o tema de redação do Enem foi "Manipulação do comportamento do usuário pelo controle de dados na internet" – enquanto a Universidade de Chicago pediu que os candidatos escrevessem sobre "Qual objeto o mundo está deixando de lado e você acha que deveríamos manter?".

Entre os milhares de comentários da publicação, muitas pessoas afirmam que as propostas são muito mais fáceis do que as exigidas no Brasil e que pareceriam "testes de internet".

👉Mas especialistas ouvidos pelo g1 explicam que, na verdade, não se trata de nível de dificuldade e, sim, que o processo de ingresso no Ensino Superior nos EUA é totalmente diferente do Brasil.

"Enquanto no Brasil o processo de admissão é majoritariamente baseado em provas, como o Enem, a Fuvest e outros vestibulares, nos Estados Unidos as universidades consideram um conjunto muito mais amplo de informações sobre o candidato", explica Gabriela Marcon, Prep Program Coordinator & Application Specialist da Fundação Estudar.

Assim, além de não possuir um exame unificado para aplicação para universidades (entenda mais abaixo) , as instituições americanas avaliam o histórico escolar, as atividades extracurriculares, as cartas de recomendação e as redações, entre outros elementos.

O primeiro ponto destacado pelos especialistas na comparação dos dois modelos de seleção para o Ensino Superior é que o aplicado nos Estados Unidos tende a ser muito mais holístico do que o brasileiro, ou seja, considera diferentes aspectos da trajetória acadêmica, das experiências e do potencial de cada estudante .

"Essa abordagem é uma característica marcante do sistema de Ensino Superior americano, embora os critérios específicos e o peso atribuído a cada componente variem consideravelmente entre as instituições", avalia Rosie Falcon-Shapiro, Program Manager of International Education & Head College Counselor da Fundação Estudar.

Ainda que não haja uma prova nacional, como o Enem, uma das formas de avaliação dos alunos é por meio de exames padronizados – sendo o SAT (Scholastic Assessment Test) e o ACT (American College Testing) os principais.

"O SAT e o ACT enfatizam a capacidade de aplicar conhecimentos, pensar criticamente, analisar informações e resolver problemas. Os estudantes precisam ter uma boa formação em inglês e matemática, mas não se espera que memorizem livros específicos, acontecimentos históricos ou fatos isolados", analisam as profissionais da Fundação Estudar.

Também diferentemente do que acontece no Brasil, essas provas são administradas por organizações independentes e sem fins lucrativos , e não pelo governo ou pelas próprias universidades. Além disso, nenhuma das duas exige redação.

Outro ponto destacado pelas especialistas é que nem todas as universidades exigem as notas desses exames em seu processo de ingresso.

"Esses exames são utilizados, quando aplicável, como mais um indicador da preparação acadêmica do estudante e de sua capacidade de acompanhar os estudos em nível universitário. [...] Um estudante com uma nota muito alta pode ser rejeitado, enquanto outro com uma nota mais baixa pode ser aprovado", destaca Marcon.

A ideia principal é que, no processo de admissão americano, a preparação acadêmica do estudante é avaliada por meio de diferentes componentes da candidatura.

O histórico escolar, as matérias cursadas, as cartas de recomendação e as atividades extracurriculares ajudam a universidade a entender não apenas o desempenho acadêmico do candidato, mas também seu potencial de contribuição para o ambiente universitário.

Nesse contexto, as redações exigidas pelas universidades americanas normalmente tendem a ser menos padronizadas e mais pessoais, justamente porque buscam, acima de tudo, conhecer o aluno que pretende ingressar na instituição.

"O objetivo não é simplesmente demonstrar habilidade de escrita ou conhecimento sobre determinado assunto, mas permitir que as comissões de admissão conheçam melhor quem é o estudante, como ele pensa, quais experiências contribuíram para sua formação e o que ele pode agregar à comunidade universitária", comenta Shapiro.

➡️A principal redação que os estudantes escrevem é chamada de personal statement :

É considerada um componente central do processo de candidatura nos Estados Unidos.

É enviada a todas as universidades que requerem esse elemento às quais se candidatam.

Em vez de responder a uma pergunta acadêmica específica, os estudantes escolhem entre uma série de temas amplos que os incentivam a refletir sobre suas experiências, seu desenvolvimento pessoal, sua identidade, seus desafios, seus interesses ou algum aspecto significativo de sua trajetória.

Tem como objetivo contar uma história que revele algo importante sobre a pessoa por trás do histórico acadêmico.

"Um dos aspectos mais interessantes dessa avaliação é justamente compreender quem é o estudante como indivíduo e cidadão. Isso permite à universidade identificar a contribuição que ele poderá trazer para o ambiente acadêmico e a diferença que poderá fazer dentro da sala de aula", destaca Larissa Teles Rocha, gerente do STB Universidades.

Além desse texto de motivação pessoal, muitas universidades consideradas mais seletivas exigem as supplemental essays (redações complementares).

➡️A quantidade de perguntas e o tamanho das respostas variam consideravelmente de uma instituição para outra. Esses temas também podem mudar a cada ano, muitas vezes refletindo as prioridades da universidade e as características que ela busca identificar em sua próxima turma.

Uma dessas instituições é justamente a Universidade de Chicago, que aparece no post que viralizou e que, segundo as especialistas, é um exemplo particularmente interessante.

"Sua candidatura geralmente inclui uma pergunta sobre por que o estudante deseja ingressar na universidade, além de uma redação mais extensa em resposta a um de seus temas criativos e pouco convencionais. Essas perguntas ficaram famosas por sua natureza inusitada e, às vezes, aparentemente excêntrica", detalha Gabriela.

As propostas podem convidar os estudantes a explorar uma questão intelectual inesperada, inventar algo ou abordar um conceito cotidiano a partir de uma perspectiva completamente diferente.

Mas a ideia não é simplesmente testar a capacidade do estudante de criar algo inusitado, e sim comunicar algo sobre a cultura intelectual da universidade .

Mesmo que as propostas criativas possam ser mais simples de executar do que os textos argumentativos normalmente exigidos em vestibulares brasileiros, os professores garantem que o processo de ingresso nas universidades americanas não é mais fácil .

Isso por conta dos pontos já colocados no início da matéria: além das notas em provas padronizadas, como o SAT ou ACT, são avaliados o histórico escolar, as atividades extracurriculares, as cartas de recomendação e as redações, ou seja, tudo conta .

Além disso, mesmo que as redações não sigam um modelo de texto mais tradicional, isso não significa que as propostas sejam simples, muito pelo contrário.

"É importante entender que propostas que, à primeira vista, parecem mais leves ou até engraçadas também exigem reflexão. Elas buscam avaliar a visão do estudante, sua capacidade de construir argumentos e a maneira como defende determinado posicionamento", pontua Rocha.

articles.title: Jovem autista é resgatado após 6 dias perdido na mata na Austrália | G1
articles.standfirst: Jovem estava em boas condições de saúde quando foi localizado por um helicóptero da polícia no leste da Austrália.
articles.summary: Jovem autista resgatado na Austrália foi localizado por um helicóptero da polícia em um leito de riacho seco após desaparecer durante um acampamento com amigo.
articles.body:
Um adolescente de 17 anos com autismo foi encontrado com vida nesta quinta-feira (12), depois de passar seis dias perdido em uma região de mata no leste da Austrália.

O adolescente, identificado pela polícia apenas como William, havia ido acampar com um amigo também adolescente quando desapareceu na última sexta-feira, perto de Walhalla, uma antiga cidade de mineração de ouro localizada 185 quilômetros a leste de Melbourne, informou a polícia.

A tripulação de um helicóptero da polícia o encontrou em meio à mata, deitado no leito seco de um riacho. Mais tarde, ele se reuniu com a mãe. William estava animado e, em geral, em boas condições de saúde, segundo comunicado da polícia.

“Estou simplesmente radiante por ele estar vivo”, disse sua mãe, Elizabeth, a jornalistas. A AP decidiu não divulgar o sobrenome dela para evitar a identificação de seu filho.

“E ele nunca mais vai sair de casa. Está de castigo para o resto da vida. Nunca mais vai a lugar nenhum”, brincou.

William foi posteriormente levado a um hospital para que seu estado de saúde fosse monitorado, informou a polícia.

O clima de primavera no Hemisfério Sul esteve ameno na última semana na região onde William se perdeu, e houve pouca chuva.

Elizabeth havia deixado o filho e o amigo no local na última sexta-feira para que passassem o fim de semana acampando. William caminhou uma curta distância do acampamento até o local onde haviam sido deixados para buscar mais equipamentos de camping, mas não voltou para encontrar o amigo, segundo a polícia.

A ampla operação de busca realizada pela polícia contou com a participação de serviços de emergência e voluntários.

articles.title: Qual é o risco de doença grave nos olhos por uso de Ozempic e Mounjaro que gerou alerta de agência dos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: O FDA afirma que canetas usadas para perda de peso devem conter informações sobre a condição, conhecida como Naion.
articles.summary: O FDA afirma que canetas usadas para perda de peso devem conter informações sobre a condição, conhecida como Naion.
articles.body:
A FDA, agência reguladora de medicamentos dos Estados Unidos, determinou que os fabricantes de canetas para perda de peso da classe dos agonistas de GLP-1 devem incluir em suas bulas alertas sobre aumento de risco de uma condição ocular grave associada ao uso dos medicamentos.

Os fabricantes de Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro e Zepbound devem alertar sobre os riscos relacionados à neuropatia óptica isquêmica anterior não arterítica, também conhecida pela sigla Naion.

Essa doença ocorre quando os vasos sanguíneos que irrigam os nervos ópticos ficam obstruídos, privando-os de oxigênio.

A condição pode causar diminuição indolor da visão em um dos olhos, que pode ser permanente, segundo a FDA.

Em comunicado à BBC, a Academia Americana de Oftalmologia afirmou que "qualquer risco adicional parece pequeno, e não foi comprovado que esses medicamentos causem Naion".

"Os medicamentos GLP-1 oferecem benefícios importantes para pessoas com diabetes, obesidade e doenças cardíacas, portanto, nossa mensagem para os pacientes é simples", disse o grupo. "Não interrompa a medicação sem consultar seu médico e, se notar perda repentina e indolor da visão em um dos olhos, procure um oftalmologista imediatamente."

No Brasil, a Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) investiga 13 notificações de suspeita de cegueira entre pessoas que usam canetas emagrecedoras.

Em junho de 2025, a agência emitiu um alerta sobre a Naion como evento adverso muito raro associado à semaglutida e determinou a inclusão desse risco nas bulas de medicamentos que contêm o princípio ativo.

Não existe tratamento conhecido para reverter a perda de visão causada pela Naion. De acordo com os especialistas, essa é a causa mais comum de lesão aguda do nervo óptico em pessoas com mais de 50 anos.

A FDA afirmou ter realizado uma análise detalhada de relatos de Naion em usuários de GLP-1, bem como uma revisão de outros estudos, e concluiu que existe um "risco aumentado de eventos raros de Naion" em pessoas que tomam esses medicamentos.

Em comunicado, a Novo Nordisk, fabricante do Wegovy, um dos medicamentos para perda de peso mais populares, afirmou acreditar que os dados "não estabelecem uma relação de causa e efeito".

"Reconhecemos que a Naion pode ter um impacto profundo nos pacientes e em suas famílias. A segurança do paciente é uma prioridade máxima para a Novo, e continuamos monitorando a segurança de nossos medicamentos", afirmou o fabricante.

As 'canetas emagrecedoras' modificaram a forma como a obesidade é tratada nos consultórios — Foto: Getty Images/BBC

De acordo com a agência reguladora americana, algumas pesquisas foram difíceis de analisar porque pessoas que tomam medicamentos GLP-1 para obesidade e diabetes tipo 2 podem já apresentar fatores de risco para Naion independentemente dos medicamentos.

A FDA afirmou que não se sabe por que aqueles que tomam medicamentos GLP-1 podem ter maior risco de desenvolver a doença ocular.

Os medicamentos já possuem advertências em seus rótulos para diversas outras condições, incluindo pancreatite e doenças da vesícula biliar.

Alguns dos sintomas mais comuns associados à semaglutida — um ingrediente fundamental em muitos medicamentos da classe do GLP-1 — incluem náuseas, vômitos e dor de estômago.

No ano passado, um órgão de segurança da Agência Europeia de Medicamentos, que faz parte da União Europeia, afirmou que até 1 em cada 10.000 pessoas que tomam semaglutida podem ser afetadas por Naion.

Em um estudo publicado há dois anos, que analisou 17.000 pacientes, pesquisadores americanos descobriram que aqueles que tomavam semaglutida tinham quatro vezes mais probabilidade de serem diagnosticados com Naion do que aqueles que não tomavam o medicamento.

Mas um dos autores do estudo, o professor de Oftalmologia da Escola de Medinina de Harvard, Dr. Joseph Rizzo, afirmou que as descobertas eram "significativas, mas provisórias", e que mais pesquisas eram necessárias sobre a relação entre o medicamento e a condição ocular em uma população mais diversificada.

articles.summary: Deputados do Pará na COP31 participam de debates sobre a Amazônia na Turquia, mas a Alepa não divulgou os custos da viagem nem a agenda oficial dos parlamentares.
articles.body:
Ao menos seis deputados estaduais do Pará participam da COP31, na Turquia. — Foto: Divulgação/Alepa

Ao menos seis deputados estaduais do Pará participam da COP 31, em Antália, na Turquia , segundo informou a Assembleia Legislativa do Pará (Alepa) ao g1 . As discussões começaram na segunda-feira (9) e seguem até 20 de novembro .

Entre os nomes informados estão o presidente da Casa, Chicão (União Brasil), e representantes de comissões e órgãos ligados a meio ambiente, cultura, infância, turismo e direitos das mulheres.

Segundo a Alepa, os parlamentares acompanham debates sobre sustentabilidade, desenvolvimento regional e políticas públicas voltadas à Amazônia. A instituição afirma que a participação dá continuidade às discussões da COP30, realizada em Belém , em 2025.

A Assembleia não detalhou os custos da participação nem as agendas individuais dos deputados. Também não informou se a comitiva se restringe aos seis parlamentares mencionados.

Veja os nomes e as respectivas áreas de atuação, de acordo com a Alepa:

Chicão (União Brasil): presidente da Assembleia Legislativa. Sua atuação institucional contempla discussões sobre ciência, tecnologia, inovação, transição energética, infraestrutura sustentável e financiamento climático

Maria do Carmo (PT) : presidente da Comissão de Meio Ambiente, Recursos Hídricos e Desenvolvimento Sustentável.

Lívia Duarte (PSOL): presidente da Comissão de Cultura, área que a Alepa associa à valorização dos conhecimentos tradicionais, à diversidade cultural e à proteção dos povos amazônicos.

Andréia Xarão (MDB) : vice-presidente da Comissão de Defesa da Primeira Infância, Criança e Adolescente. Sua atuação está relacionada aos debates sobre justiça climática e proteção das populações vulneráveis.

Fábio Figueiras (PV): membro titular da Comissão de Turismo e Esporte, área vinculada ao turismo sustentável, à economia verde e ao desenvolvimento regional.

Paula Titan (PP): presidente da Procuradoria da Mulher da Alepa, com atuação na promoção dos direitos das mulheres, na igualdade de gênero e nas políticas de proteção feminina.

Durante duas semanas, a conferência reúne representantes de quase 200 países, além de cientistas, ambientalistas, empresários e integrantes da sociedade civil, para negociações sobre o futuro da ação global contra as mudanças climáticas.

articles.title: A 4.3-hectare wetland in England uses 350,000 plants from 52 species to treat wastewater and storm overflows; the nature-based engineering system has cut embodied carbon by 60%
articles.summary: Dearne Reach, a 4.3-hectare integrated constructed wetland in Clayton West, Huddersfield, treats wastewater and storm overflows with plants rather than
articles.body: Dearne Reach, a 4.3-hectare integrated constructed wetland in Clayton West, Huddersfield, treats wastewater and storm overflows with plants rather than pipes. According to the Institution of Civil Engineers (ICE), a traditional solution would have needed 7,000 m³ of stormwater storage and a 4.5km pipeline. Instead, over 350,000 plants from 52 species, set in 13 cells, take nutrients from the water to help improve quality along 4km of the River Dearne. Mott MacDonald Bentley delivered the £14 million project for Yorkshire Water in nine months. ICE reports a 60% reduction in embodied carbon and a 40% reduction in operational carbon across its lifecycle.How has the nature-based wetland reduced embodied carbon by 60%ICE states that a traditional "grey" infrastructure solution would have required 7,000 m³ of stormwater storage and a 4.5km pipeline to divert treated wastewater downstream. According to ICE, the wetland instead uses natural processes to reduce pollution, particularly of un-ionised ammonia, which the page describes as highly toxic to aquatic life, and to improve storm flow treatment.ICE reports that Mott MacDonald Bentley was principal designer and contractor, Yorkshire Water was the client and Stantec produced the outline design. The source says that at 4.3ha this is currently the largest integrated constructed wetland for storm treatment in the UK. According to ICE, the project won the Centenary Award at the 2026 ICE Yorkshire and Humber Awards.How does the wetland treat unpredictable stormwater dischargesAccording to ICE, the 52 plant species sit in 13 cells, and over 350,000 plants adsorb nutrients from storm overflow discharges and from wastewater flowing out of the Clayton West wastewater treatment works. ICE adds that "adsorb" means the nutrients attach to the plants rather than being absorbed. The wetland is divided into multiple cells, each designed to hold water for longer and remove pollutants more effectively.ICE states that the wetland was specifically designed to treat intermittent storm overflows. The source says traditional ICWs are only effective when there is a constant flow of water, whereas this design can handle the unpredictability of stormwater discharges. According to ICE, solar-powered monitoring equipment controls water levels and measures flow rates, and it collects data on water quantity and quality that will support future development of similar nature-based solutions.How did the wetland project reduce embodied carbon by 60%ICE reports that the project achieved a 60% reduction in embodied carbon and a 40% reduction in operational carbon across its lifecycle. According to the source, the site presented high groundwater levels and difficult ground conditions in the form of sandy-gravelly clay, alongside a need to reuse more than 13,000 m³ of excavated material. ICE says groundwater management techniques allowed cell heights to be increased, which improved the balance between excavation and fill material and reduced the need to import material.ICE lists several further measures taken during construction. The amount of bypass pipework was reduced through maintenance planning, lowering the carbon footprint. A geosynthetic clay liner was used instead of more carbon-intensive plastic alternatives to provide impermeability and protect groundwater. According to ICE, Roadcem soil stabilisation technology replaced traditional concrete access roads, reducing the need for imported aggregates and cutting carbon emissions.How did AI technology improve construction efficiency at the wetlandAccording to ICE, the project model and programme were uploaded into the Smart Construction and Earthbrain software platforms before construction began. The source says these tools use artificial intelligence to determine the most efficient construction methods, identify the size and number of machines required, and optimise the movement of excavated material. ICE describes this as a first-of-its-kind trial of intelligent plant technology on a nature-based solution project. The site team reported that model-led excavation reduced unnecessary earthworks and supported a "right first time" approach, and that automated systems decreased manual surveying and limited interactions between people and plant. ICE adds that precision excavation enabled the efficient movement of 65,000 m³ (117,000 tonnes) of soil.ICE states that seven planting zones were created using 350,000 locally sourced plants, resulting in a 38% biodiversity net gain for terrestrial habitats. The team also worked with the local council to improve a public right of way by creating a 2m-wide wheelchair-accessible footpath around the wetland. ICE says the project demonstrates how nature-based solutions can provide effective, low-carbon stormwater management, and that its design and delivery are helping to advance sustainable approaches across the water industry.You use AI every day. articles.title: Sonam Wangchuk removed from protest site, escorted home by Ladakh Police amid hill council poll row
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: Ladakh Police late Wednesday evening removed Leh Apex Body member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk from a protest site and escorted him to
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Ladakh Police late Wednesday evening removed Leh Apex Body member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk from a protest site and escorted him to his residence.The police action came hours after Wangchuk, along with leaders of the Leh Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) voiced concern over the decision to hold hill council elections on December 4, citing harsh winter conditions and migration of around 25% from Ladakh to other parts of the country.“In compliance with the prohibitory orders issued by the Chief Electoral Officer, UT Ladakh, and the District Magistrate, Leh, regulating public rallies, protests and other public gatherings within the limits of Leh Municipality in view of the ongoing election exercise, Ladakh Police has today taken preventive action by removing Sonam Wangchuk from the protest site and escorting him to his residence,” a police statement issued early Thursday morning said.“Sonam Wangchuk has been advised to stay at his residence. The action has been taken in exercise of the powers vested in the competent authority under the prevailing prohibitory orders, with the objective of preventing any potential breach of public order and maintaining peace and tranquillity,” the police said.“The general public is advised to strictly adhere to the prohibitory orders in view of the Panchayat, Municipal and LAHDC elections in Ladakh and refrain from any activity that may disturb public peace and law-and-order,” officials added.The Ladakh administration Wednesday imposed a complete ban on protests and demonstrations within the municipal limits of Leh and Kargil, citing the municipal and hill council polls scheduled for November 23 and December 4, respectively.Ladakhi leaders including Wangchuk had announced protest against the decision saying it is unprecedented in Ladakh history to conduct an election in harsh winter when around 25% Ladakhis are out of the region.“Ladakh is known as the world's coldest inhabited place. The weather forecast for December indicates snowfall. How will elections be conducted in such conditions? Half of the population is outside Ladakh, while students are already studying in different cities. When Leh, Kargil and other areas are nearly empty, why are you holding elections,” Wangchuk had said on Wednesday evening in an online briefing along with other Ladakh leaders.On Tuesday the region’s State Election Commission (SEC) announced elections for the eight autonomous hill development councils (LAHDC) in the Union Territory, with polling scheduled for December 4.The announcement for Ladakh Panchayat election and Municipal bodies was made earlier and they are scheduled to be held on November 21.On Wednesday, the office of the chief electoral officer issued an order stating that the model code of conduct has been enforced and will remain in force till the completion of the election process.The order said organising of political dharnas, protests, demonstrations, sit-ins, rallies or similar collective activities within the municipal limits of Leh and Kargil during the currency of the model code of conduct has the potential to intimidate voters, disturb public order, and vitiate the atmosphere for free and fair elections:On Tuesday Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra described LAHDCs polls as a watershed moment and turning point for Ladakh democracy.“I personally feel that this is a watershed moment for Ladakh and democracy in Ladakh. It's a turning point. And I think it is a crucial inflection in the larger journey of democracy,” Kundra said addressing a press conference in Leh after the SEC issued election notification.Defending the timing of December 4 for polls, the CS had said schools remain open in Ladakh till December 15. “If children can go to school during this period, I don't think there should be any difficulty for adults to come out and vote,” he said.He further said deputy commissioners have been instructed to ensure adequate facilities at polling stations, particularly for elderly voters.“We have assured that all deputy commissioners have been instructed to provide necessary facilities at polling stations. Heaters will also be provided and separate queues will be arranged for elderly voters so that they do not face any inconvenience,” he added.Stay updated with the latest Srinagar news. articles.title: Boy, 4, falls into sewer in Delhi’s Ranhola, mutilated body located at water plant
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A four-year-old boy who fell into a nearly 50-foot-deep sewer in Outer Delhi’s Ranhola area on Tuesday was found dead after an almost 20-hour
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A four-year-old boy who fell into a nearly 50-foot-deep sewer in Outer Delhi’s Ranhola area on Tuesday was found dead after an almost 20-hour search operation.His dismembered body was recovered around 3.5 km from the spot where he had fallen, at a water treatment plant in Nilothi, police said.Preliminary information suggests that the child, Imran, a resident of Som Bazar Wali Gali in Mohan Garden, had accompanied his mother to Dass Garden Park.He reportedly moved towards the drain to attend to nature’s call when he accidentally fell into an open manhole alongside the service road. The manhole was allegedly covered with a thin fibre sheet.Cops said information about the incident was received at Ranhola police station at 3.20pm, following which a team rushed to the spot near Kheri Baba Pul.Delhi Fire Services personnel and teams of NDRF launched a joint rescue operation. However, the family has alleged that the initial search remained confined to the spot where the boy had fallen until Wednesday morning.According to the family, the boy fell into the sewer at 3pm. They claimed police reached the spot at 5pm, while NDRF personnel arrived between 6pm and 7pm. The family alleged the teams initially focused on the immediate vicinity of the accident site and didn’t trace the sewer route.The sewer is an underground, narrow passage through which sewage flows towards the treatment plant. The family said the boy’s body was eventually found at the Nilothi plant, around 3.5 km downstream from the point where he fell.A police officer said the body was located after the flow of water through the sewer was stopped. Manholes along the route were the only access points to the underground sewer, the officer said.The recovery has added to the family’s anguish. The boy’s father identified him by his hands, which had become separated from the body. The family said it had not yet seen the child’s face.The remaining body parts were brought to Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital in a cloth bundle for preservation and post-mortem examination.Police have registered a case under Section 106(1) of BNS, which deals with causing death by negligence. Further investigation is underway to establish the circumstances of the incident and determine responsibility.Speaking to TOI, a rescuer said the teams reached the spot soon after receiving information about the incident. “It was a difficult rescue operation as we had to open the covers of individual manholes along the sewer route. Entering the sewer was also challenging because of the presence of toxic gases. Rescuers had to use breathing apparatus sets to enter,” the rescuer said.More than 50 personnel were involved in the operation, he said. “During the night, we used searchlights to inspect the sewer as visibility was extremely poor. The process was time-consuming. Eventually, the teams reached the point where the sewer flow terminated, and the boy’s body was found there. It was an unfortunate outcome,” he added.According to a DJB official, information was received at 5.22 pm from an executive engineer (maintena­nce), DJB, that a child had fallen into a manhole of a sewer line in Nangli Vihar. The staff rushed to the spot and found cops, along with the NDRF team, had already initiated rescue operations.The site was also inspected by DJB officials. It was observed that the interceptor sewer line passes beneath the closed boundary wall of Najafgarh Drain, which falls under the jurisdiction of irrigation and flood control department.The cover of the concerned sewer manhole was found damaged. It was stated that all manhole covers installed along the interceptor sewer line are secured with nuts and bolts and cannot ordinarily be removed without appropriate tools.It was also submitted that entry into this stretch had been prohibited by police, and that a woman and a child had entered this area at 1.30pm Tuesday, following which he fell into the sewer.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: ‘LinkedIn Premium subscriptions, MacBooks and more’: Canva CEO offers ‘different’ support package after announcing major job cuts
articles.summary: Australian design software company Canva recently announced that it is cutting 1,271 jobs, roughly 22% of its global workforce, as it grapples with
articles.body: Australian design software company Canva recently announced that it is cutting 1,271 jobs, roughly 22% of its global workforce, as it grapples with slowing growth and prepares for a major internal overhaul. Co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins broke the news in a lengthy message to staff, which was later published on the company’s newsroom website. Perkins apologised to affected employees for the pain and disruption caused by the restructuring. The cuts will touch teams across all 37 countries where Canva operates. While many employees will be asked to move into new roles or relocate to centralised office hubs, others will be leaving the company. To those leaving, the company has offered a support package that may be different from others. What’s in Canva’s support packageTo soften the blow for departing staff, Canva outlined an extensive severance and support package. Regardless of where they live, employees leaving the company will receive at least six months of salary (including statutory entitlements) and up to 12 months of healthcare coverage, where applicable.Along with this, the company is offering departing workers to keep their Canva-issued MacBooks. Moreover, they will receive LinkedIn Premium subscriptions, alongside access to an alumni talent network, and access to career coaching and interview preparation for career help. Canva is also launching the “Canva Collective Fund,” which will offer$10,000 grants to eligible departing employees who want to start their own businesses or community projects.Read the message by Canva CEO:Supporting those who are leavingWe know everyone's circumstances are different, and while nothing can make today’s news easy, we've tried to reflect those different needs in the financial, career and wellbeing support we're providing to everyone affected:•Everyone will receive at least six months of salary, inclusive of statutory entitlements, regardless of location. •Removing the one-year vesting cliff for those who joined in the past year. •Twelve months of continued healthcare coverage in countries where we currently provide this. •Twelve months of Canva Care (our EAP), with this coverage also extending to family members. •Dedicated career support, including one-on-one coaching, interview preparation, and one year of LinkedIn Premium. We're also dedicating a significant portion of our Talent Acquisition team to helping people review their resumes and practice for interviews to find their next opportunity. •An opt-in alumni talent directory that we'll proactively share with our investors, partners, and wider industry network to help connect departing Canvanauts with new roles. •Everyone leaving will be able to keep their Canva MacBook as we know not everyone has a personal laptop. We’re also launching the Canva Collective Fund, providing US$10,000 grants to departing Canvanauts who want to start something of their own. Whether it’s starting a business or doing something meaningful for their local community, the fund is designed to help get those ideas off the ground. Everyone leaving as part of these changes will have until the 14 of December to register their interest, and we won’t take any ownership or equity in what they create.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1976, Michigan fifth-graders buried a class time capsule; when former classmates reunited 50 years later, they found only cloth scraps, rusty metal and glass
articles.summary: In a nostalgic reunion, former Michigan fifth-graders discovered that their 1976 time capsule had deteriorated into scraps after being buried for 50 years, but the event rekindled cherished memories.
articles.body: Most of us probably have a box somewhere we meant to open one day. For a group of Michigan classmates, that box sat underground for 50 years. As Katy Snodgrass of the Huron Daily Tribune reported, former Sebewaing students gathered at their old school to dig up the class time capsule they buried back in 1976 as fifth-graders. They hoped to find what they had left behind. Instead, they found only scraps of cloth, bits of rusty metal, and jagged pieces of glass. Not much of the capsule remained, but the day brought old friends together.A reunion planned from across the countryFormer Sebewaing school student Tina Blanco, who moved west in 1978, led the effort. Now living in San Diego, she organised the reunion from across the country before flying to Michigan for the event. Her older sister, Lamia Shoreez, also made the trip, along with classmate Lee Johnson and Dan Rummel, the son of the teacher who buried the capsule. Many others came to help as well. Some of them had ties to the capsule, while others came simply because they wanted to see what all the hype was about. Blanco recalled that her fifth-grade teacher, Erma Rummel, arranged the time capsule back in April 1976. Classmates brought things to put inside that day, but most were looking forward to reading the letter Rummel had written.Digging through the debris The old school has since become Bayview Garden Assisted Living, but the time capsule remained undisturbed on the property where the students had left it. With permission and assistance from staff, Blanco and a small group of observers watched as workers began to dig out the plaque that was supposed to protect the capsule. Around 1:00 PM, workers arrived with a shovel and began digging. A fifth-grader, the son of a worker, helped too, in honour of the fifth-graders who had buried the capsule. After a few minutes of digging, it was clear that the capsule was no longer intact. Blanco and the onlookers urged the workers to continue digging through the debris, pulling out anything of note, unwilling to give up.Why time capsules break down The article doesn't say why the capsule fell apart; therefore, no one can be sure about what exactly caused the incident. However, conservators and activists have investigated why closed time capsules often fail. The Library of Congress explains that a good time capsule needs a good container, a good place to keep it, and careful choices about what goes inside. Unstable materials will continue to break down even inside the best container, and bad material will influence others negatively because of the confined space they occupy. In his report, ‘Notes on Time Capsules,’ R.L. Barclay from the Canadian Conservation Institute notes that copper sheet and tinplate on 19th-century capsules fostered an acidic environment inside, which could damage the contents. For new capsules, he says, stainless steel is by far the best material and advised keeping the inside free of oxygen and water as much as possible.Memories that outlasted the box In the end, it was a letdown. But the search had brought back memories that had survived what was in the ground. The trip was a chance for Blanco and her sister to revisit part of their childhood. The classmates did not receive the mementoes for which they came, but they did get to reunite at their own school 50 years after the capsule went into the ground. articles.title: In 2011, San Francisco sewer workers found two ships buried 15 feet underground; their cargo routes and reused timbers revealed how the city filled its shoreline and replaced sail-powered trade
articles.summary: In 2011, sewer workers in San Francisco discovered two historic ships buried underground, shedding light on the city's shoreline evolution and the transition from sail-powered trade to modern shipping.
articles.body: Imagine a sewer crew digging a trench and hitting a ship. That's what happened in San Francisco in early February 2011. Archaeologists monitoring a sewer improvement project in the Sunnydale neighbourhood of Visitacion Valley found two vessels, a scow schooner and a barge, according to the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC). Both were buried about 15 feet or 4.5 metres below the ground. When found, both were more than a hundred years old.A routine job takes a strange turn The idea behind this project was to upgrade old sections of the sewer pipe. Archaeologists from the Far Western Anthropological Research Group were present at the location to watch for any signs of the past history of the city. Then a backhoe pulled up wooden pieces, and the project was put on hold for some time. Historical archaeologists R. Scott Baxter and Rebecca Allen, working with Environmental Science Associates, discovered posts, planks, a support beam, and large pieces of wood. Maritime museum staff came over and confirmed what the team suspected. They had uncovered a portion of a scow schooner. The stern, or back end, lay inside the trench, but the bow or front end, remained buried outside it. Soon the archaeologists found a second ship nearby, a wooden barge.The flatbed trucks of the bayThese two ships helped supply San Francisco in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The utility’s write-up notes that the scow schooner probably carried hay, lumber, and bags of salt, while the barge may have carried barley, wheat or anything else the growing city needed. The National Park Service described a real-life example in the scow schooner Alma, built in 1891. It recorded that she carried hay and lumber under sail. In 1918, her masts were removed, and she was towed as a barge, hauling sacks of salt. Jim Delgado, the author of Gold Rush Port: The Maritime Archaeology of San Francisco’s Waterfront, described scow schooners as flatbed trucks of San Francisco Bay. He added that they are largely forgotten now, yet they moved the goods that built the city and the Bay Area economy.How the shoreline grew over the wrecksThe team studied the site to find out more about how and why the ships were buried. For thousands of years, the site, located on the western side of San Francisco Bay, was underwater. It was the floor of a small cove which Native Americans likely used to harvest oysters and other food items. During the Gold Rush era, the area was still submerged. However, as the city expanded, so did its shoreline, since fill and other debris were dumped into the bay. With the emergence of railroads and cars, which became the means of delivery of cargo instead of ships, abandoned ships started accumulating around the shores of San Francisco. A photograph taken from the air in 1938 showed that the small cove to the south of Candlestick Point had already been filled in. Many abandoned ships were visible, anchored to the east. Near the cove, a ship of about the same size as the scow schooner found in 2011 was also visible, and the agency's page suggests it could be the same vessel.Recycled one last timeBack in the 1930s, Candlestick Cove was a ship-breaking site. Ships were beached and stripped of valuable wood, metal and other recyclable materials. The wrecks were often burned and abandoned, crumbling into rubble to form new land. Both ships were what was left of broken, salvaged vessels. The timbers were waterlogged and decayed rapidly when exposed to air. So, the archaeologists had to record both ships in place, noting construction details and learning about building techniques. Team leader Dr Brian Byrd called the discovery an exciting and important once-in-a-lifetime experience. As the SFPUC frames it, the discovery captured a moment of change, when railroads, trucks, and automobiles replaced scow schooners and barges.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Why Nvidia stopped telling investors about Singapore sales after cutting off Alice Huang-linked Megaspeed
articles.summary: Nvidia quietly stopped reporting its Singapore revenue in late 2025, months after it cut off Megaspeed International, the Singapore-based cloud company
articles.body: Nvidia quietly stopped reporting its Singapore revenue in late 2025, months after it cut off Megaspeed International, the Singapore-based cloud company now at the heart of the espionage scandal around CEO Jensen Huang. The timing, flagged by The Wall Street Journal, raises fresh questions about how much investors could see of Nvidia’s sales tied to a market that was briefly one of its biggest.In the quarter ending July 2025, Singapore brought in $10.2 billion, or 22% of Nvidia’s total revenue, up 81% from a year earlier. Two years before that, its share was just 8%. A quarter later, the line had vanished from Nvidia’s filings. An Nvidia spokesperson told the WSJ that Megaspeed was put on an internal block list in June 2025, barring further sales and shipments. The company has not said whether the two moves are connected.Nvidia switched from billing address to headquarters for country-wise revenueFrom the quarter ending October 2025, Nvidia began assigning revenue by where a customer is headquartered rather than where it is billed. It said the change “provides a better representation of the geographic profile of our revenue.”The old breakdown listed the US, Singapore, Taiwan, China (including Hong Kong) and “other”. The new one kept every line except Singapore. Recast figures suggest most Singapore-billed revenue moved into the US column, while China and Taiwan were revised higher.The WSJ points to a hole in that logic. Nvidia had earlier said Singapore was used mainly for centralised invoicing, with products “almost always shipped elsewhere.” A headquarters address says no more about where chips land. Nvidia spokesperson Patrick Rutherford declined to say where Megaspeed’s sales were booked under either method, or whether dropping Singapore was linked to the block.Servers from US firms like Dell and Super Micro add another layer. Many buyers get Nvidia chips inside these systems, and it is unclear whether those deals count as US revenue wherever the machines end up.Megaspeed probe and Alice Huang affair now threaten Jensen Huang’s jobIn August 2025, between the block and the reporting change, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter emailed Commerce Department agents investigating Megaspeed, saying a senior department official had cleared him to reach out, according to The New York Times. The case was soon handed to the Justice Department, which is running a criminal inquiry. In October 2025, President Trump was briefed that Megaspeed executive Alice Huang was presumed to be a Chinese intelligence asset close to Jensen Huang, the NYT reported.Trade records cited by the NYT show Megaspeed’s Malaysian sister firm Speedmatrix bought at least $4.8 billion of AI equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, well past the June 2025 cutoff and often through intermediaries. Megaspeed denies illegally moving chips to China.Huang has since admitted the affair and apologised to employees. Nvidia’s board is investigating whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, and the WSJ has reported that the board is preparing to oust him.Without a Singapore line, Nvidia’s filings cannot show whether cutting off Megaspeed dented sales or barely registered. Either answer would have invited the questions the company is now facing anyway.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In Oregon’s 1993–95 trial across 21 sites, crews sprayed liquid magnesium chloride before freezing rain to keep ice from bonding; two applications cost $24 per lane-mile, 75% less than sand
articles.summary: Discover how Oregon's use of liquid magnesium chloride for winter road maintenance significantly reduces costs and environmental impact. The 1993-1995 study revealed a proactive approach to managing icy roads, proving to be a game changer for highway safety and maintenance.
articles.body: A hazard of frozen precipitation on highways has long bedevilled highway maintenance crews, especially in areas where a sudden plunging temperature can turn a wet highway into a sheet of ice. But Oregon Highway managers considered a different approach to wintertime highway treatment in a test from 1993 to 1995. Instead of using mostly sand to coat icy roads, highway crews pretreated roads with liquid magnesium chloride before the snow and ice arrived. The solution was supposed to keep the ice from fusing to the pavement, therefore allowing highway crews to more easily plough the ice off the roads after the winter storm stopped. The compound was tested at 21 sites and could offer a cheaper alternative to conventional winter road treatment.Oregon shifts from winter sanding to preventive anti-icingAccording to the Oregon Department of Transportation, when the snow and ice melted after the long and bitter winter of 1992-1993, the mud and sand that coated the roads turned out to be a serious problem. ODOT conducted a survey that estimated that 50% to 90% of the sand applied to roads during winter storms remained, washing off the roads and ending up along the shoulders, in streams, and in culverts and ditches. Some of the sediment also contributes to water pollution, and many of the trucks and machinery that applied the sand created dust problems for adjacent residences.The strategy shifted from reacting after ice formed to a preventive technique called anti-icing, the document says. In simple terms, road crews could spray a freezing-point depressant before ice formed so snowploughs could remove the frozen precipitation more easily. That way, ploughs could clear the frozen precipitation from the road, reducing the need for repeated applications of sand and chemicals. But it required crews to check forecasts and pavement conditions before ice had a chance to form.A 21-site experiment reveals substantial cost savingsDuring the winter of 1993-1994, Oregon DOT experimented with anti-icing strategies at 21 check sites in nine districts. The sites chosen ranged from city streets to mountain passes and rural roadways with minimal traffic. The range of sites let officials observe how the strategies performed under different conditions. The test extended into the winter of 1994-1995. Two different liquid chemicals were tested in the experiment. One notable aspect of the experiment was the impact of liquid magnesium chloride when it was applied prior to freezing rain. While crews normally wait for ice to form, a few roads were salted beforehand to discourage the hardened precipitation from sticking to the pavement.According to the Federal Highway Administration, two applications of liquid magnesium chloride in a freezing rain storm cost roughly $24 per lane mile. Applying sand three times costs about $96 per lane mile, making the magnesium chloride treatment about 75% cheaper. The savings went beyond the cost of materials. Traditional sanding also needed labour, equipment and transportation, and the remaining sand that was swept up after storms had to be removed from the sides of roads, ditches and channels.How the technique influenced winter road maintenanceThe technique was part of a broader move toward pre-treating highways for winter maintenance. In 1996, the FHWA published a manual of practice for an effective anti-icing program after analysing the 1993-1995 winter seasons in 15 participating states. The manual emphasised the need for weather information to determine the appropriate level of chemical to be applied and the need for maintenance personnel to be ready to take action. It also explained that certain types of weather were more appropriate for liquid treatment, depending on pavement temperature, the amount of precipitation, and the possibility of the chemical being diluted or washed off.A study published in Transportation Safety and Environment found that chemical de-icers significantly impact the environment. Researchers pointed out the importance of protecting sensitive aquatic systems and also evaluating the impact of chemicals after they have been deposited on the landscape. Oregon learned that winter road maintenance does not need to start only when the pavement is covered with ice. Using a pre- treatment strategy, highway crews could eliminate the need for sand, reduce cleanup, and minimise treatment expenses. The experiment helped validate the use of a preventive road treatment strategy.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Between 1942 and 1977, Shenandoah National Park ranger Roy Sullivan was struck by lightning seven times and survived each one, a feat that earned him a Guinness World Record for most lightning strikes survived
articles.summary: A lightning strike is usually a terrifying, potentially fatal encounter. For Roy Sullivan, it became an extraordinary recurring experience.
articles.body: A lightning strike is usually a terrifying, potentially fatal encounter. For Roy Sullivan, it became an extraordinary recurring experience. The Virginia park ranger was struck by lightning seven times between 1942 and 1977, surviving every incident and earning a place in Guinness World Records as the person who survived the most lightning strikes. His encounters left him with burns, singed hair and injuries, and eventually earned him the nickname “Spark Ranger”, according to Guinness World Records.Sullivan’s first brush with lightning came in April 1942, when he was working at Shenandoah National Park in Virginia’s Blue Ridge Mountains. He was at a fire lookout tower when a storm set the structure ablaze. As he attempted to escape, lightning struck him in the right leg. The bolt left a scorch mark, tore through his boot and damaged the nail on his big toe.It was an experience that might have made most people wary of storms for the rest of their lives. Sullivan, though, would encounter lightning six more times over the next 35 years.A series of increasingly bizarre encountersFor 27 years after the first incident, Sullivan reportedly went without another strike. That changed in July 1969, when he was driving his truck along a mountain road during a storm. Lightning struck trees nearby before travelling through the vehicle’s open windows. Sullivan was knocked unconscious, his eyebrows were burned and his wristwatch was damaged.The following year, in July 1970, lightning struck him while he was tending to his garden. The bolt reportedly burned his left shoulder and threw him off his feet. In April 1972, another strike hit while he was working inside a park guardhouse. His hair caught fire, forcing him to put it out with water.By then, Sullivan had begun taking precautions. According to a 2013 Washington Post profile, he carried water with him after the incident in which his hair caught fire. But avoiding storms and taking shelter did not appear to end his extraordinary run of misfortune.On August 7, 1973, lightning struck him again while he was driving. Sullivan later said he had stopped after trying to get away from a storm, only to see a bolt coming towards him. The strike set his hair alight, burned his legs and reportedly knocked him out of his vehicle.The sixth incident occurred on June 5, 1976, while Sullivan was walking along a trail. He suffered an ankle injury and his hair was burned once more. Five months later, he retired from the National Park Service. He and his wife moved to a property near Waynesboro, Virginia, where he installed copper lightning rods around his home, including on the trailer, television antenna and nearby trees. Still, the precautions did not bring his encounters to an end.The seventh strike and a world recordOn June 25, 1977, Sullivan was fishing when lightning struck him for the seventh time. He reportedly smelled sulphur and felt the hair on his arms stand up moments before the bolt hit. The strike burned his chest and stomach, singed his hair and damaged his hearing in one ear. He managed to reach his car and return home, after which he was taken to hospital.Guinness World Records lists this as his final lightning strike. Its record entry documents seven incidents, beginning in 1942 and ending on June 25, 1977. Sullivan was subsequently recognised as the person who had survived the most lightning strikes.His story attracted attention well beyond the national park. He appeared on television programmes and became a familiar name in accounts of unusual survival stories. The nickname “Spark Ranger” followed him, while his lightning-damaged hat and wristwatch became part of the lore surrounding his experiences.A shocking taleSullivan’s record is recognised by Guinness World Records, but the details of his encounters have also attracted questions. A 2013 investigation by The Washington Post noted that none of the seven strikes was directly witnessed by another person. His wife and fellow rangers were not present for the incidents, and there was no medical record independently confirming every strike.The report found that newspaper accounts and statements from people who knew Sullivan offered some support for his injuries. His family doctor and a former park superintendent were said to have verified injuries, though not necessarily the lightning strikes themselves. A retired National Park Service historian interviewed for the report expressed confidence in the Guinness record, while others who knew Sullivan were more cautious.Sullivan died in September 1983, aged 71. His story remains an unusual chapter in the history of Shenandoah National Park and a reminder of the unpredictable power of thunderstorms.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: After moving his hedge fund from Chicago to Miami in 2022, billionaire Ken Griffin bought every one of 138 apartments in a downtown condominium; now he is reshaping the city through massive investments and donations
articles.summary: When billionaire hedge fund manager Ken Griffin decided to move his financial empire from Chicago to Miami in 2022, it was seen as another high-profile
articles.body: When billionaire hedge fund manager Ken Griffin decided to move his financial empire from Chicago to Miami in 2022, it was seen as another high-profile endorsement of Florida's growing appeal to wealthy investors and businesses. Four years later, his presence in the city has become considerably more significant than anticipated. Griffin has bought all 138 residential apartments in a downtown condominium tower, is backing a multibillion-dollar corporate headquarters and has committed billions to education, healthcare and other causes.According to a Financial Times report, Griffin has spent more than $5.3 billion on property, business infrastructure, philanthropy and political contributions since relocating to South Florida. The Citadel founder's investments have made him one of the most influential private figures in the region, with supporters pointing to the jobs, institutions and development his money could bring.From Chicago to Miami: A financial empire changes baseGriffin announced in June 2022 that Citadel, his hedge fund, and Citadel Securities, its electronic trading business, would move their headquarters from Chicago to Miami. The decision followed years of frustration with conditions in Illinois, including concerns about crime and the state's political leadership. The relocation was expected to take place over several years, with the companies planning to establish a major office presence in Miami's Brickell financial district.The move was not Griffin's first investment in South Florida. He had already shifted some employees to the region during the Covid-19 pandemic and purchased a waterfront property on Star Island. But the headquarters announcement marked a more permanent commitment, bringing the prospect of jobs, business activity and other wealthy financial professionals to the city.His real estate ambitions have since expanded beyond a private residence and office space. In July 2026, Bloomberg reported that Griffin had acquired all 138 residential units at Solaris, a 22-storey condominium tower in Brickell. The purchases were made through a network of limited liability companies, with offers arriving individually and residents initially uncertain about who was behind them.Some owners accepted the offers, while others held out for better prices. The acquisition was part of Griffin's broader effort to assemble property around the site of his planned headquarters. The building's location makes it significant to his wider development plans.A $2.5 billion headquarters and a bigger visionOne of Griffin's largest projects is a new Citadel headquarters in Brickell, estimated to cost about $2.5 billion. The proposed 54-storey development at 1201 Brickell Bay Drive is expected to become a major addition to Miami's skyline. The project is being developed with Related Companies, while Citadel and Citadel Securities plan to occupy a substantial portion of the office space.The headquarters is part of a wider effort to establish Miami as a major centre for financial services. Griffin's relocation has helped attract attention from businesses and wealthy professionals considering South Florida, although the city's growth cannot be attributed to one individual alone.Billions for education, healthcare and researchGriffin's influence extends beyond commercial property. Through his philanthropic initiative, Griffin Catalyst, he has directed substantial sums towards education, medical research and community projects.In September 2026, he announced a gift of more than $3 billion to Carnegie Mellon University, one of the largest individual donations in the history of higher education. The contribution will help establish a new campus in Miami, while also supporting the university's existing operations in Pittsburgh. The Miami campus is expected to focus on fields including healthcare and biological discovery, national security, energy and climate resilience, and advanced manufacturing.His earlier donations in South Florida include $50 million to the University of Miami's Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center for cancer research and another $50 million to Baptist Health South Florida to support neurological care and research into conditions such as Alzheimer's disease. He also gave $25 million to Nicklaus Children's Hospital for a new surgical tower and supported Miami-Dade public schools, scholarships and community projects.A billionaire's rising influenceBut Griffin's growing role in Miami has also brought scrutiny. The Financial Times report highlighted concerns about political influence, development decisions and the accountability that comes with private wealth shaping public life. His political contributions, which the report puts at more than $60 million, have added to questions about the relationship between wealthy donors and local decision-making.The debate is unfolding as Miami and the wider South Florida region grapple with housing affordability and inequality. The arrival of wealthy residents and businesses has helped fuel investment, but rising housing and living costs have also made it harder for some existing residents to remain in the area.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A leaking bathroom sink can be a nuisance at home.
articles.body: A leaking bathroom sink can be a nuisance at home. But when it happens thousands of feet in the air, with nowhere to escape the mess, it can quickly turn into an emergency. Passengers aboard a Frontier Airlines flight from Denver to Detroit experienced just that on Wednesday, when a burst bathroom faucet flooded the aircraft's cabin and forced the pilots to divert to Chicago.According to a post by The New York Post, Frontier Airlines Flight 3566 was travelling to Detroit when the sink in its forward lavatory reportedly sprang a leak. Water began spilling across the floor and flowing down the aisle, soaking the cabin.Concerned that the water could reach the aircraft's electronic systems, the pilots declared an emergency and requested permission to land at Chicago O'Hare International Airport.“Mayday, mayday, mayday,” a pilot told air traffic controllers, according to audio broadcast by LiveATC.net.Explaining the situation, the pilot said: “We’d like to declare an emergency, our forward lav sink has sprung a leak, and it’s spraying so much water that it’s flooding the entire cabin area in the back, and we are worried about electronics.”The crew then requested a diversion to Chicago O'Hare instead of continuing to Detroit.Video shows water flooding aircraft aisleFootage recorded by a passenger and obtained by ABC7 showed water spreading across the aircraft's aisle, leaving a large section of the cabin floor soaked.Images shared by Keegan Morris on Facebook also showed water leaking from the bathroom area and pooling on the floor.The visuals captured the extent of the flooding inside the aircraft, which prompted the pilots to seek an emergency landing over concerns about water reaching the plane's electronics.You use AI every day. articles.title: A new Orlando Health survey finds nearly 60% of Americans more worried about foodborne illness in 2026; ahead of Thanksgiving, doctors warn about the common turkey-washing practice that can spread bacteria
articles.summary: The holiday season is around the corner, which means family dinners, crowded counters and a turkey that has to be ready on time.
articles.body: The holiday season is around the corner, which means family dinners, crowded counters and a turkey that has to be ready on time. This year, the kitchen might be the most important place to get things right. Doctors are paying attention to what happens before the oven door even opens, and one habit that many cooks consider a step towards cleanliness is now the one they want retired.A new national survey from Orlando Health found that nearly 60% of US adults are more worried about foodborne illness this year than in previous years. “2026 has been an extraordinarily bad year for food safety, especially in terms of the number of outbreak cases and the volume of recalls by weight. With the holiday season approaching, it’s crucial to stay alert, especially when it comes to how food is prepared, served and stored.”Americans are on high alert for foodborne illnessThe new survey found that more than half of US adults are concerned about food safety as the holiday season arrives.Dr Daniel Egan, MD, a physician with Orlando Health Medical Group’s Infectious Diseases practice, says the alarming list of pathogens shouldn’t send anyone into a panic; however, awareness is crucial. “It sounds scary to hear about all of these different bacteria or these new infections, E. coli, Salmonella, Cyclospora, Campylobacter, Giardia, but in reality, they’re not new. We’ve treated them before. If you’re more aware of them, you’re also going to take more steps to prevent those kinds of infections.”Safety precautions to follow while cooking, serving and storing foodDr Egan recommends some safety practices that people can follow to stay safe, especially while preparing meals and storing leftovers.Wash your hands between tasks: Take a moment to wash your hands between tasks. Using soap and water each time you switch activities, whether you’re moving from raw turkey to the stuffing bowl, coming back from the bathroom or cooking while feeling unwell, is among the simplest ways to keep germs from spreading throughout the meal.Never wash or rinse raw poultry: Rinsing raw turkey in the sink feels like cleaning, but it mostly spreads bacteria. Water splashes onto counters, plates, utensils and the sink itself. Cooking is what kills the germs, so the bird doesn’t need a bath first. “Do not rinse raw turkey or chicken in the sink,” the doctor says.Prevent cross-contamination with separate tools and storage: Give raw meat its own cutting boards, prep dishes and utensils, separate from serving platters and anything ready to eat. In the fridge, cover raw meat and store it on its own shelf or in its own drawer, away from produce and leafy greens.Use a food thermometer to check internal temperatures: During the festive season, avoid relying on visual inspection alone. Use a thermometer probe to ensure your turkey and other meats reach a safe internal temperature. This keeps them out of the danger zone, where bacteria multiply.Rinse produce and leafy greens, even pre-washed items: “Pre-washed” doesn’t mean untouched. Bacteria can be picked up during transport and handling, so run fresh produce under running water before it reaches the table, including bagged greens. Put in that extra effort to avoid a trip to hospital.Keep food covered and track how long it sits out: Keep serving dishes covered to guard against dust and pet hair. Don’t let perishable food sit out for longer than one to two hours. Then pack the leftovers into airtight containers and put them in the fridge.Take extra care during the holidaysYou might be cooking every day, but holidays are different. They come with their own health risks. “Holiday cooking is unique compared with your normal daily or weekly cooking. When cooking large meals, you might skip a few steps here and there to try to be more efficient. But that increases your risk of transmitting infection,” Dr Egan explained.How a stomach bug can land you in hospital? The symptoms of foodborne illnesses include vomiting, nausea, cramps, diarrhoea and fever. They can appear anywhere from six hours to several days after exposure. Mild cases that clear within a day can usually be managed at home. Young children, older adults, pregnant women and people with weakened immune systems face the greatest risk of complications such as dehydration and kidney problems. Dr Egan advises seeing a doctor if symptoms worsen or persist.“If it resolves within a day, then it’s resolved. If it’s not going away or it’s even escalating, your body is losing fluids; it’s losing electrolytes. We can do testing to see if there’s anything wrong with your electrolytes and if there’s any particular infection that needs antibiotics.”Do not take foodborne illnesses too lightly. Foodborne diseases sicken 48 million Americans annually, leading to 128,000 hospitalisations and 3,000 deaths, according to US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Meg Powel, 33, of Columbus, Ohio, says she takes the necessary steps, regardless of the current outbreak, to protect her family from foodborne illnesses. “I would never want that to happen in my own house, in my own kitchen, so I really try to be as careful as possible. Using disposable gloves, a good produce wash, airtight containers, a food thermometer and multiple cutting boards. At the end of the day, if I’m the one serving everything, then I take full responsibility for making sure everyone is really taken care of.”Thanksgiving still belongs at the table. But remember, the bird just needs to stay out of the sink.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Can't wait for firing to stop': Farooq Abdullah bats for India-Pakistan talks despite twin terror attack
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah on Thursday advocated dialogue between India and Pakistan, saying meaningful engagement between
articles.body: NEW DELHI: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah on Thursday advocated dialogue between India and Pakistan, saying meaningful engagement between New Delhi and Islamabad must begin without waiting for hostilities to end.Talking to reporters, Abdullah asserted that bullets and military confrontation cannot resolve political disputes."Ab aap intezaar karenge, jab tak aap sabki goliyan band ho jayengi, tab tak raat ho jayegi (If you keep waiting for everyone to stop firing, it will be too late by the time the guns fall silent)," Abdullah said."I have always told Pakistan to stop terrorism. Nothing can be achieved through terrorism. The process of dialogue must begin because only through talks can a way forward be found," he added.The former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister also called for the revival of SAARC, saying regional countries must come together to resolve their differences and work towards collective progress."India is the largest country in the region, and Indira Gandhi had shown the way for India to maintain cordial and sympathetic relations with neighbouring countries. We must revive SAARC so that all of us can sit together, resolve our disputes and work towards progress and development," he said.Reacting to the recent twin terror attacks in Kulgam and Kishtwar districts, which claimed the lives of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) and left three CRPF personnel injured within two days, Abdullah asserted that those harbouring ambitions of taking Kashmir must abandon such notions. He also said that terrorism would never succeed in its designs.However, he expressed concern over claims in Delhi that terrorism had ended in Jammu and Kashmir, maintaining that the recent incidents indicated that the threat persisted and that concrete measures were needed to eliminate it."I have already said such incidents are still happening. One never knows where the next attack might take place," he said.This comes days after Abdullah courted criticism for his remarks that Pakistan's repeated efforts to raise the Kashmir issue internationally were putting pressure on India.He alleged that the Centre's intentions towards Jammu and Kashmir were not good and urged people to stand up for their rights.“What can you expect from Delhi? You must have the courage to stand up to them and fight. If you do not, you will be wiped out. Your name and identity will disappear, and no one will even remember you. Our neighbour (Pakistan) is constantly after them. It goes everywhere, saying that the Kashmir issue has not been resolved. It is protecting us; otherwise, their intentions are not good. They say one thing but do something entirely different,” Abdullah said.He also called on people to stand by the truth, warning that their future would remain insecure unless they spoke out.“You must have the courage to stand by the truth. Speaking the truth is not easy, but unless you speak the truth and stand firm by it, your future will never be secure,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'No light, no water, no heat: Kyiv faces 20-hour blackouts as Russian strikes cripple Ukraine's power grid
articles.summary: For millions of Ukrainians, the fight to survive Russia's war is increasingly being fought inside their own homes, in darkness and freezing cold.
articles.body: For millions of Ukrainians, the fight to survive Russia's war is increasingly being fought inside their own homes, in darkness and freezing cold.In Kyiv, where Russian strikes have pushed the power supply close to critical, families are racing against the clock to cook meals, finish homework and charge their phones before the next blackout.According to a BBC report, some households in Kyiv are facing power cuts lasting up to 20 hours, with electricity available for just four to five hours a day in some areas. The outages have disrupted heating, water supplies and public transport, leaving residents struggling as temperatures continue to fall.For Daryna Kulchytska, a single mother living in a seventh-floor apartment in Kyiv, every evening has become a race against the next blackout."There is no light, no water, no heat, no electricity. And no fun. All the fun got sucked out with the electricity," her 12-year-old son Kyryll told the BBC.The family often turns to torches, LED candles and board games when the power goes out. But even these offer little comfort to children who have already played the same games countless times.The crisis extends far beyond individual households. Kyiv has been among the worst-hit areas, with electricity shortages disrupting metro services and bringing trolleybuses to a standstill at times.Across Ukraine, hundreds of thousands of people have been left without power in recent weeks as Russian attacks continue to damage energy facilities. The current round of scheduled outages began earlier than last winter and has lasted longer, raising concerns about the country's ability to maintain essential services as temperatures drop.The BBC reported that Ukrainian officials are concerned that life could become unsustainable for millions if electricity supplies cannot be maintained for at least four hours a day. Some families in Kyiv are already experiencing outages of up to 20 hours, forcing residents to adjust their daily routines around unpredictable electricity schedules.Russia has intensified its campaign against Ukraine's energy infrastructure since August, targeting power stations and critical electricity facilities ahead of winter.The BBC reported that a ballistic missile strike on one of Ukraine's largest power stations left it completely offline, with turbines buried under rubble and machinery reduced to twisted metal.The attacks have also made restoration work increasingly difficult, with repair teams repeatedly forced to seek shelter during air raid alerts. Russia has also been using so-called "waiter drones" that attach themselves to electricity pylons and cables before detonating.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Tarot Card of the Day, November 12: The Chariot Meets Mars — Are You Ready to Take Back Control of Your Direction?
articles.summary: The Chariot is the Tarot Card of the Day for November 12.
articles.body: The Chariot is the Tarot Card of the Day for November 12. It stands for willpower, focus, forward motion and control gained by holding opposing forces together. Mars moves out of its weak placement, which restores drive and nerve, so effort that felt heavy for weeks may start to carry weight again.Today may bring a surge of resolve after a flat stretch. A stalled task could look doable. A hard decision may feel less frightening.The Chariot Tarot Meaning for November 12The Chariot: Signifies progress that comes from steering with a firm hand.A figure in armour stands in a square chariot under a starry canopy. Two sphinxes, one dark and one pale, rest in front, each facing a different way. There are no reins. The driver holds them in line by purpose alone.It is a card of earned momentum.The card asks where effort has been scattered. A plan started in three directions, a savings goal abandoned after one bad month, or a course dropped halfway are ordinary examples. And speed means little until the pulling forces agree on one destination.Mars Leaves Its Weak PlacementMars is connected to courage, drive and action. In Cancer, a sign of caution and emotion, it loses force and tends to hesitate or react defensively. Moving out of that sign lets the planet work with more directness.So the zodiac now favours decisive steps taken in order. Choose the task that matters most. Start it before noon.But renewed energy can outrun judgement. Check the facts before a bold move, and stay calm when others slow things down.Steering Before SpeedingA returning surge of strength is best spent on direction first. Write the goal in one line. Cut anything that does not serve it.Then set the first action for today, not next week. Small, visible progress rebuilds trust in one’s own effort.Love and RelationshipsThe Chariot: Two people pulling the same way may move further than either expected.Couples could agree on a shared aim, such as a move, a savings target or a trip, and divide the tasks clearly. Decide who does what, and by when. A vague promise tends to fade.Singles may feel more confident about acting on interest in someone. Make the first move plainly and without pressure. Accept the answer calmly, either way.Anger may rise faster than usual. Pause before replying to a message that stings.Career and MoneyNovember 12 suits launching a delayed project, asking for responsibility or pushing a negotiation forward. Prepare the figures first, then speak with confidence.If a deadline has slipped, set a new date and tell everyone involved. A clear plan restores credibility.Money: Execute a decision you have been postponing, such as starting a fixed monthly saving or closing an unused account. A bill is due and needs to be paid today. Don’t get all cocky all of a sudden and spend on risky things.Are You Ready to Take Back Control of Your Direction?Likely, if your goal is clear and you've already planned small steps. The Chariot shows the discipline, and Mars leaving its weak placement supplies the energy to use it.The question for November 12 is: Which one task would change the week if it were finished today?Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates.
